newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Costello no comment on rate timetable.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Costello no comment on rate timetable.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello on Friday would not be drawn on the timing of the next change in monetary policy, saying instead consumers should take advantage of interest rates which were already at 30-year lows.

Costello, interviewed on the Seven Network's 11 AM programme, said he did not want to take part in the guessing game of financial markets about exactly when the official cash rate would next be altered by the Reserve Bank of Australia.
"Rather than trying to do the guessing game, let's just look at the real benefits that are in place for consumers and let's make sure that we can get the best benefit to home buyers."

A large number of financial market economists had predicted that the central bank could lower the 5.5 percent official cash rate at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) on Friday, the time it usually announces rate changes. It last cut the cash rate on May 23 from 6.0 percent.
The predictions were based on low second quarter inflation and wages data issued earlier this week.
